page: UpCloud PREMIUM-2xCPU-2GB is an x86_64 architecture server powered by an AMD EPYC 9575F processor. It features 2 shared vCPUs running at 2.0 GHz, with 2 physical cores and 1.0 thread per core. The hardware configuration includes 2.0 GB of system memory, providing 1.0 GB of RAM per core, alongside a bundled 50 GB local SSD storage volume. The CPU is equipped with 16 MB of L3 cache, 0.5 MB of L2 cache, and 64 KB of L1d cache. It supports advanced instruction sets including AVX-512, AVX_VNNI, and AVX512_BF16, as well as cryptographic acceleration via AES, VAES, and SHA_NI.

Benchmark data reveals a stark contrast between single-core and multi-core performance. In single-core execution, the server achieves top-tier results, with stress-ng single-core CPU performance scoring 3787.27 and single-threaded gzip compression reaching 40.69 GB/sec, both placing in the top 10%. However, multi-threaded and memory-intensive workloads show clear limitations. The PassMark memory score is poor, placing in the bottom 10%, while multi-threaded bzip3 decompression and PassMark database operations fall into the bottom 25%. Redis SET operations are also weak at 6.18 million operations per second, reflecting the constraints of the shared CPU allocation and limited memory capacity.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the server offers high single-thread compute capability relative to its resource class, though its shared CPU model and low memory density limit its utility for sustained parallel processing. It is suited for lightweight workloads that benefit from strong bursty single-core performance but do not require large memory footprints, such as basic static web serving, simple text processing, or lightweight background tasks.
description: The UpCloud PREMIUM-2xCPU-2GB is an x86_64 server featuring 2 shared vCPUs from an AMD EPYC 9575F processor, 2.0 GB of RAM, and 50 GB of local SSD storage. Operating on the KVM hypervisor, this instance delivers top-tier single-core performance, as evidenced by its stress-ng single-core score of 3787.27 and high single-threaded compression speeds. However, its shared CPU allocation and low memory capacity result in poor memory bandwidth scores and weak multi-threaded database performance. This server is a cost-efficient option for lightweight, single-threaded workloads, static web serving, and basic utility tasks that do not demand high memory density or sustained multi-core execution.
